openapiOps.title: Acquire a cloud recording resource
openapiOps.description:
Gets a cloud recording resource ID. Before starting cloud recording, call `acquire` to get a resource ID. One resource ID can be used for only one recording session.

To improve the success rate, call `acquire` and `start` in pairs and call `start` within two seconds after receiving the resource ID. The resource ID is valid for five minutes and should be used as soon as possible.

openapiOps.title: Start cloud recording
openapiOps.description: Starts cloud recording by using a resource ID returned from `acquire`. After calling `start`, check that the recording service has started successfully before relying on the recording output.

openapiOps.title: Update cloud recording settings
openapiOps.description:
Updates cloud recording settings during an active recording session. For individual and composite recordings, use this endpoint to update subscription lists. For web page recording, use it to pause or resume recording or to update the CDN streaming address.

The request is valid only within a recording session. If you call `update` successively, send the next request only after receiving the previous response.

openapiOps.title: Update the cloud recording layout
openapiOps.description:
Updates the mixed video layout for composite recording. Each call overrides the original layout settings. If you omit a field that was previously set, the service uses that field's default value.

The request is valid only within a recording session. If you call `updateLayout` successively, send the next request only after receiving the previous response.

openapiOps.title: Query cloud recording status
openapiOps.description: Queries the status of a cloud recording session. The request is valid only within a recording session. If the recording was started incorrectly or has ended, the request returns `404`.

openapiOps.title: Stop cloud recording
openapiOps.description:
Stops a cloud recording session and makes the recording service leave the channel. To start recording again after the recording stops, call `acquire` again to request a new resource ID.

The request is valid only within a recording session. In non-web page recording modes, if the channel is idle for longer than the configured duration, Cloud Recording automatically leaves the channel and stops recording.

openapiOps.title: Acquire a builder token
openapiOps.description:
Before you create a Cloud Transcoding task, call the `builderTokens` endpoint to retrieve a builder token. An `instanceId` can generate multiple builder tokens, but only one token can be used to initiate a request in a task.

## Reference

Note the following guidelines when using a `builderToken`:

- After calling this endpoint successfully, you receive a `builderToken` in the response body. You can use a `builderToken` for a single Cloud Transcoding task.
- The validity period of a `builderToken` for creating Cloud Transcoding is 5 minutes. To ensure successful Cloud Transcoding, best practice is to initiate the corresponding `Create` request within 2 seconds after each `Acquire` response is received.
- Making batch `Create` requests after batch `builderToken` requests may cause the request to fail.

**Output destination constraints**

- A single transcoding task cannot push to both a CDN address and an RTC channel simultaneously. To push to both destinations, create two separate tasks.
- If the audio or video configurations differ between the two destinations, create two separate tasks.
- To push to multiple CDN addresses, include all destination addresses within a single `outputs` object.
- Each transcoding task can push to only one RTC channel. To push to two different RTC channels, create two separate tasks.

openapiOps.title: Create a cloud transcoding task
openapiOps.description:
Creates a Cloud Transcoding task. When the task starts, Agora transcodes the specified input streams and outputs the result to the specified Agora RTC channel.

## Reference

Note the following guidelines when using a `builderToken`:

- After calling the `Acquire a builder token` endpoint successfully, you receive a `builderToken` in the response body. You can use a `builderToken` for a single Cloud Transcoding task.
- The validity period of a `builderToken` for creating Cloud Transcoding is 5 minutes. To ensure successful Cloud Transcoding, best practice is to initiate the corresponding `Create` request within 2 seconds after each `Acquire` response is received.
- Making batch `Create` requests after batch `builderToken` requests may cause the request to fail.

**Output destination constraints**

- A single transcoding task cannot push to both a CDN address and an RTC channel simultaneously. To push to both destinations, create two separate tasks.
- If the audio or video configurations differ between the two destinations, create two separate tasks.
- To push to multiple CDN addresses, include all destination addresses within a single `outputs` object.
- Each transcoding task can push to only one RTC channel. To push to two different RTC channels, create two separate tasks.

openapiOps.title: Update a cloud transcoding task
openapiOps.description:
Updates an existing Cloud Transcoding task. The request body must contain all fields from the `Create` request body. For fields that you do not need to update, use the original values.

## Reference

The `Update` request supports modifying the following fields only:

- Add or delete `rtc` members in `audioInputs[]` and `videoInputs[]` to subscribe or unsubscribe from the host's audio and video streams.
- Modify the `region` field in `videoInputs[]` to update the host's combined picture layout.
- Modify the `audioOption` and `videoOption` fields in `outputs[]` to update the transcoding output audio and video configurations.

openapiOps.title: Delete streaming key
openapiOps.description:
Deletes a streaming key. After a streaming key is deleted, you can no longer use it to push streams. If the deleted streaming key is still in use, the ongoing stream is not affected. To disable the ongoing stream immediately, delete the streaming key and then force disconnect the stream by SID.

This API can also revoke streaming keys generated by a script. For complete key revocation, call this API across all configured regions.

openapiOps.title: Query streaming list
openapiOps.description: Queries current Media Gateway ingress streams. If you specify a channel, the response only contains streams in that channel. Because Agora channel names support special characters, URL-encode the channel name before sending the request.

openapiOps.title: Query streaming information
openapiOps.description: Queries an ongoing stream by SID. A streaming session ID is generated for each initiated streaming task. You can obtain the SID by querying the streaming list or by receiving the message notification callback.

openapiOps.title: Force disconnect
openapiOps.description:
Disconnects an ongoing stream by SID. You can combine this API with the Delete streaming key API to disable a stream.

Delete the streaming key first. Otherwise, after this API disconnects the stream, the streaming software may immediately reconnect, creating a new push session and a new SID.

openapiOps.title: Mute or unmute streaming
openapiOps.description:
Mutes or unmutes the current stream.

A successful response only confirms that the command is sent to the gateway node handling the stream. It does not guarantee that the mute/unmute operation has completed. The operation is executed asynchronously in the background and typically takes effect within about one second. If the operation does not work as expected, retry the API call.

Each stream starts unmuted by default. Each API call applies to the current stream. If the streamer disconnects and restarts the stream, the new stream resets to the initial unmuted state.

openapiOps.title: Create or reset template
openapiOps.description:
Creates or resets a flow configuration template. In the template, you can configure transcoding parameters for video or audio streams and parameters for mitigating network latency.

Up to 10 flow configuration templates can be created under an app ID, each with a unique template ID. Specify the template ID when creating a template. If a template with this ID already exists, the existing template is reset with the incoming request body.

You can use flow configuration templates in two ways: specify a global template for the app ID, or specify a configuration template for a specific streaming key. By default, a template is not set for the app ID, and video transcoding is not enabled.

openapiOps.title: Update template
openapiOps.description:
Updates a flow configuration template. This API can only be called when the template already exists.

Changes to a flow configuration template take effect only after the stream is pushed again. Because synchronization between the gateway and database can be delayed, wait 3 minutes after calling this API before pushing the stream again.

The supported update fields are `transcoding.video`, `transcoding.audio`, and `jitterBuffer`. These fields are independent. For example, if you only want to update `transcoding.video.fps`, pass the entire `transcoding.video` object with the modified `fps` field and the other fields unchanged.

openapiOps.title: Delete template
openapiOps.description:
Deletes a flow configuration template. The stream currently being pushed with the template is not affected and continues to use the template parameters. The deletion takes effect from the next push, including normal push and disconnection/reconnection.

If the template associated with the streaming key is deleted, the global template under the app ID is used by default. If no global template is configured, the stream uses the no-template setting and video transcoding is not enabled.

openapiOps.title: Set global template
openapiOps.description:
Sets a global flow configuration template, which applies to all streaming keys under the app ID. Create a flow configuration template before calling this API.

For beta users, this API previously could also set transcoding parameters. Agora recommends using the template creation API instead. If you previously used this API to set `transcoding`, resetting `defaultStreamTemplate` makes the previous `transcoding` setting invalid and the new template parameters take effect.

openapiOps.title: Query notification service IP address
openapiOps.description:
Queries the IP addresses of Agora message notification service. If your server is behind a firewall, call this API and configure your firewall to trust the returned IP addresses.

Agora adjusts message notification service IP addresses every 24 hours. Best practice is to call this endpoint at least every 24 hours and automatically update the firewall configuration.

### Client callbacks for `join_channel` bans

- Windows: The `onConnectionStateChanged` callback reports `CONNECTION_CHANGED_BANNED_BY_SERVER(3)`.
- Electron: The `AgoraRtcEngine.on("connectionStateChanged")` callback reports `3`.
- Unity: The `OnConnectionStateChangedHandler` callback reports `CONNECTION_CHANGED_BANNED_BY_SERVER(3)`.
- React Native: The `ConnectionStateChanged` callback reports `BannedByServer(3)`.
- Flutter: The `ConnectionStateChanged` callback reports `BannedByServer(3)`.
- Cocos Creator: The `onConnectionStateChanged` callback reports `CONNECTION_CHANGED_BANNED_BY_SERVER(3)`.
- Applets: `on(event: "client-banned")`.

openapiOps.title: Get user events
openapiOps.description:
Gets the user login and logout events from the address specified by the Agora Signaling server. Events you acquire using this API are removed from the server; you cannot retrieve the same event twice.

The Signaling backend stores a maximum of 2,000 events, with the latest event replacing the oldest when this limit is exceeded. The backend returns a maximum of 1,000 events per request, and the number of requests for each app ID must not exceed 10 per second.

> Agora does not guarantee event time sequence across geographical regions. Events pulled from different regions may contain duplicates since synchronization only occurs within regions, not across them.
